acceptedAnswer.text: Marketing attribution is the practice of linking outcomes — revenue, pipeline, conversions — back to the inputs that produced them, so spend and effort can be directed at what actually works.

Causal attribution goes beyond correlation. It identifies which inputs actually cause outcomes, controlling for the other inputs that happened nearby in time. It's the difference between 'this channel was touched' and 'this channel made the deal'.

mainEntity.name: How do small businesses know which marketing works?

acceptedAnswer.text: Run every metric through three filters — Meaningful, Actionable, Profitable. Then compare cohorts that received an input against cohorts that didn't. If you can't construct the comparison, the metric isn't yet ready to drive spend.
